findings.title: The shipped-defaults test cannot read what the serializer returns
findings.whats_wrong: This test is the only automated guard over 71 hand-written default values, and it fails on its very first comparison — for three separate reasons the plan does not anticipate. The engine's serializer hands back nested Maps, not plain objects, and the plan's path-walking helper steps a path with an operator that never sees a Map entry. The serializer also lowercases every key, while the shipped table uses mixed-case paths. And it reports enum values as numbers, while the shipped table stores their names. The step then tells the implementer to believe the failure and take the engine's value — so correct shipped defaults get rewritten to nothing. The plan anticipates only a fourth trap, about packed colour integers.
findings.proposed_fix_narrowed: Rewrite the test to match the serializer's real output: convert the returned Map tree to plain objects, lowercase each path segment before reading, and resolve an enum row's stored name to the number the serializer reports. Then exclude ONLY the three keys that genuinely cannot match a fresh engine instance — the player mode, the scroll offset, and the rendering engine — each with a one-line reason.
